title: First surviving term is preserved under agreement on fixed variables
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables — a list of terms, each a conjunction of literals — and let $\rho$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions of these $n$ variables. Suppose $\sigma$ agrees with $\rho$ on every variable that $\rho$ fixes, that is, $\sigma(v) = \rho(v)$ for every variable $v$ on which $\rho$ takes a Boolean value rather than leaving it free. Let $t$ be the first term of $f$ (in list order) that is not killed by $\rho$, and suppose in addition that $t$ is not killed by $\sigma$. Then $t$ is also the first term of $f$ that is not killed by $\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: σ agrees with ρ on every variable ρ fixes (ρ(v) ≠ none ⇒ σ(v) = ρ(v))
t is the first term of f not killed by ρ
t is not killed by σ
